formalizations.evidence:

Given G(A_F)=G_infty×G_f with its archimedean smooth Lie models and the finite restricted-product topology, an exact generic presentation is F:LocallyConstant G_f (ContMDiffMap I modelSelf G_infty ℂ infinity), with HasCompactSupport of (a,b)↦F b a. ContMDiffMap:41 is literally the CMDiff infinity subtype, LocallyConstant:217/IsLocallyConstant:39 imposes local constancy of the WHOLE smooth function in the finite variable, and HasCompactSupport:215 is compact closure of the support. This avoids a weaker pointwise separate-slice interpretation. Factorizable functions can be restricted to actual pure tensors of given local test functions, with characteristic functions of the chosen compact-open integral subgroups as the almost-all reference factors; the bare restricted-tensor generators-and-relations supplier was checked in036. No assertion that all test functions are a single pure tensor, nor an unproved adelic Lie-model existence theorem, is made. Interpretation required by the standard adelic test-function terminology: local constancy in the finite variable is joint/uniform for the archimedean function (equivalently the usual common finite level on compact support). The displayed constructor records that convention. Mere separate slice smoothness/local constancy is weaker and no equivalence with that weaker condition is claimed.
Search and boundary notes: Enumerated Global/Adeles, native ContMDiffMap tree and every LocallyConstant sibling. Read native LocallyConstant/Compact:26: its WHOLE X×P map is locally constant, also in the archimedean variable, so it is not the general smooth test-function API. Schwartz rapid decay and analytic Fourier/Petersson applications are different conditions/endpoints. Factorizable refers to the pure restricted generators with specified local test data, not arbitrary completed Hilbert tensors. Specification refinement: spell out the joint/uniform finite-variable convention when defining mixed archimedean/nonarchimedean test functions. Compact support alone does not justify upgrading arbitrary separate slice regularity.
